headline: Minister Ram Mohan Naidu reviews India’s preparedness for SAF and CORSIA implementation
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Minister Ram Mohan Naidu reviews India’s preparedness for SAF and CORSIA implementation

Chairs high-level stakeholder meeting on SAF production, blending roadmap and carbon accounting framework

29 JUL 2026 9:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Civil Aviation today organized a high-level stakeholder meeting chaired by Minister Ram Mohan Naidu to review India's preparedness for the adoption of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and compliance with the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), the global carbon reduction framework of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

The meeting was attended by Secretary (Civil Aviation) and senior officials from the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Airports Authority of India (AAI), Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), airlines, airport operators and other key stakeholders.

The meeting reviewed the progress made in SAF production, certification, and supply chain development across the country. The status of various SAF production projects being implemented by Oil Marketing Companies and the timelines for commissioning these facilities were also reviewed. Stakeholders deliberated on measures required to ensure the timely availability of Sustainable Aviation Fuel to meet the anticipated demand from 2027 onwards.

Speaking on the occasion, Minister for Civil Aviation Shri Ram Mohan Naidu said, “India is committed to building a robust and globally competitive Sustainable Aviation Fuel ecosystem that supports the growth of our aviation sector while contributing meaningfully to global decarbonisation efforts. Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘One Earth, One Family, One Future’, we are approaching SAF not merely as a compliance requirement but as a strategic national opportunity. Multiple stakeholders including the farmers stand to gain from the SAF value chain.”

The Minister further stated, “As an industry, we are already working on multiple fronts to reduce emissions. From 0 in 2014, today 104 airports in the country have switched entirely to 100% green energy usage. By encouraging the leasing ecosystem, airlines are being supported to have modern and fuel-efficient fleets. SAF is also a critical component for our collective efforts. We must now move from feasibility studies to concrete production timelines and from ambition to action. Every stakeholder needs to have clear obligations for ensuring adequate production as well as robust accounting. Our immediate priority is to achieve the 1% CORSIA blending requirement in the most cost-effective manner. As part of our long-term strategy, the carbon-credit offset mechanism must be developed through a whole-of-government approach.”

Shri Ram Mohan Naidu reviewed the proposed implementation roadmap for SAF blending mandate, including the roles and responsibilities of Oil Marketing Companies, airlines and airport operators. Discussions were held on establishing a robust accounting, monitoring and reporting framework aligned with ICAO/CORSIA requirements, development of a national SAF Registry with end-to-end traceability and measures to facilitate certification and market access.

Emphasising the importance of coordinated execution, the Minister said, “This transition must be driven through collective decision-making and close coordination among all stakeholders. We reviewed progress in SAF supply-chain development, the national SAF Registry, accounting and reporting systems and measures required for effective CORSIA compliance. I am encouraged by the significant progress already made and by the commitment shown by all participating Ministries and industry stakeholders. We have directed all concerned stakeholders to expedite the identified action points so that India is fully prepared well before the mandatory phase of CORSIA begins on 1 January 2027.”

Talking about the SAF Policy and the financial impact of SAF, Minister added, “The draft SAF policy is now in its final stages. So, we are doing multiple such inter-ministerial consultations and stakeholder engagements at various levels. For me voice of the passenger remains central and passenger happen to be the most important stakeholder of our industry. We have to ensure that this process imposes the least possible burden on passengers and airlines. For that we need to study all the possible SAF pathways and within pathways identify the most cost-effective mechanism right from production to drop-in at the airport”.

The meeting further deliberated on India's preparedness for CORSIA implementation, including the issuance of Letters of Authorisation and the development of a CORSIA-compliant carbon market framework in India.

The Government of India remains committed to promoting domestic production of Sustainable Aviation Fuel, strengthening India's aviation ecosystem, reducing carbon emissions from international aviation and positioning India as a global leader in sustainable aviation.

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
The Ministry of Civil Aviation organized a high-level stakeholder meeting chaired by Minister Ram Mohan Naidu to review India's preparedness for implementing Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and complying with the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), with a target implementation date of January 1, 2027.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Meeting held on July 29, 2026, attended by officials from multiple ministries, DGCA, AAI, BIS, BEE, OMCs, airlines, and airport operators
- Focus on reviewing SAF production progress, certification, supply chain development, and project timelines

- Coordination directed among all stakeholders to expedite action points before mandatory CORSIA phase begins
- Recognition of 104 Indian airports already operating on 100% green energy as part of broader emission reduction efforts

headline: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Unveils Theme for 10th Edition of India Mobile Congress 2026: ‘Scale without boundaries’
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Unveils Theme for 10th Edition of India Mobile Congress 2026: ‘Scale without boundaries’

IMC 2026 to Bring Together Global Technology Leaders, Innovators, Startups and Policymakers to Shape the Next Phase of India’s Digital Transformation

29 JUL 2026 9:39PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, today unveiled “Scale without boundaries” as the theme for the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026. The landmark edition of Asia’s largest digital technology forum is scheduled to be held from October 7–10, 2026, at Yashobhoomi (India International Convention & Expo Centre), New Delhi.

The theme launch event was also graced by Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications & Rural Development as the Guest of Honour, and Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications as the Special Guest.

The theme “Scale without boundaries” reflects India’s ambition to build a digital future where technology, innovation and connectivity transcend traditional boundaries and reach every sector, community and region. It underscores the need to take transformative technologies and solutions beyond experimentation and enable their widespread adoption, integration and impact at scale. The theme also highlights the importance of fostering collaboration among technology, infrastructure, industry, startups, academia, policymakers and consumers to create an ecosystem where innovation can scale without limitations and contribute meaningfully to inclusive growth and national development.

The 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 is anchored around four key pillars that reflect India’s vision of building a digitally empowered, secure and growth-oriented future:-

Srishti – Building the Future, which will focus on fostering innovation, emerging technologies and solutions that shape the next generation of digital infrastructure.

Suraksha – Strengthening Trust, which will underscore the importance of secure, resilient and trusted digital ecosystems.

Sashakt – Expanding Opportunities, aimed at leveraging technology to empower citizens, businesses, startups and communities while ensuring inclusive access to digital opportunities.

Samvardhan – Fueling Growth, which will highlight the role of digital technologies in driving economic growth, investment, entrepreneurship, job creation and India’s emergence as a global technology leader.

Together, these four pillars embody the spirit of “Scale without boundaries”, reflecting the ambition to take innovation, connectivity and digital transformation beyond boundaries and enable their impact to scale across sectors, geographies and communities.

As India advances towards a digitally empowered and technology-driven future, IMC 2026 will provide a platform to explore how emerging technologies and robust digital infrastructure can enable scale across sectors and geographies. The event will spotlight the convergence of technologies such as 5G, 6G, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, cloud and edge computing, satellite communications, electronics manufacturing, quantum technologies and green technologies, among others.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, said that “India’s journey in telecom has moved from connecting the next billion to enabling the next billion possibilities. The theme of the 10th India Mobile Congress, ‘Scale Without Boundaries’, reflects our ambition to ensure that the technologies we build, the standards we shape and the solutions we create in India reach new markets, communities and possibilities across the world.”

The Union Minister further emphasised that “India is no longer only a market for technology; we are increasingly becoming a nation that designs, develops and scales technology for the world. From indigenous telecom technologies and 6G standards to digital public platforms, our journey from ‘Vocal for Local’ to ‘Local for Global’ embodies the spirit of ‘Scale without Boundaries’ and our vision of building a Viksit Bharat 2047.”

Echoing the vision outlined by the Union Minister, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications & Rural Development, said that “The last 10 years has been unprecedented for Indian Telecom. IMC is an event which help us showcase to the world what India has achieved in the field of telecom. This is a place where government gets an opportunity to collaborate, startups showcase their hard work and investors find opportunities to invest.”

Highlighting the significance of the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress, Shri Amit Agrawal, Chairman, Digital Communications Commission and Secretary, Department of Telecommunications (DoT), stated that “It is a privilege to be here at 10th Edition of IMC and the journey of 10 years. This time, we are going with a much larger strategy and will showcase India’s progress in the field of telecom to the world.”

Organised by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), IMC 2026 will bring together leading global and Indian technology companies, telecom operators, policymakers, startups, investors, researchers and innovators under one platform. The 10th edition will build upon the success of previous editions and further strengthen IMC’s position as a premier global forum for discussions on the future of telecommunications and digital technologies.

The event will showcase cutting-edge innovations and use cases across emerging technologies, while providing a platform for technology demonstrations, product launches, industry collaborations, investment opportunities, knowledge exchange and policy dialogue. The flagship start-up programme ASPIRE will continue to provide emerging technology startups with opportunities to connect with investors, incubators, accelerators, industry leaders and potential partners.

With its 10th edition, IMC 2026 aims to move beyond showcasing technological advancements to examining how these innovations can be integrated, scaled and translated into real-world outcomes. The event will focus on building resilient and inclusive digital ecosystems that can empower citizens, strengthen industries, create new opportunities and accelerate India’s emergence as a global technology leader.

Marking a decade of India Mobile Congress, the 10th edition celebrates a remarkable journey that began with the aspiration to “connect the next billion”. Over the past ten years, IMC has evolved alongside India’s telecom and digital transformation, providing a platform for innovation, collaboration and global engagement. As India enters the next decade, IMC 2026 looks ahead to a larger ambition — taking Indian technologies, standards and solutions beyond boundaries and connecting the next possibilities.

The previous editions of India Mobile Congress was a huge success with over 1.4 lakh visitors, 860 exhibitors, representatives from 101countries, 1,500 Use Cases showcased, 465 startups participated, featured 918 speakers across 113 sessions, including 52 keynote addresses, 12 roundtables, and 84 panel discussions.

headline: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia confers Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia confers Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards

29 JUL 2026 9:36PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia today conferred the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards- 2025 to two organizations for their outstanding contributions in Telecom Technology. The awardees are as follows:

Amantya Technologies Pvt. Ltd.

The selection process for Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards included nomination by all Indian citizens as well as institutions registered in India through Rashtriya Puraskar Portal (https://awards.gov.in) managed by Director General, Awards at the Ministry of Home Affairs.

About Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards:

‘Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards’ have been instituted by Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, to encourage innovations in telecom sector and stimulate/ inspire Telecom Skill ecosystem by rewarding the successful telecom skilled people and institutions of India annually for their exemplary and outstanding contributions in the areas of Telecom Innovations, Telecom Skilling, Telecom Services, Telecom Manufacturing, Telecom Applications in deploying telecom dependent sectoral solutions for different fields such as agriculture, commerce, health, education etc.

headline: Innovation, Startups, MSMEs and Quality Manufacturing are Pillars of India's Future Growth: Shri Piyush Goyal at 22nd J.R.D. Tata Memorial Lecture
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Innovation, Startups, MSMEs and Quality Manufacturing are Pillars of India's Future Growth: Shri Piyush Goyal at 22nd J.R.D. Tata Memorial Lecture

₹1 Lakh Crore RDI Fund, India-AI and Second Semiconductor Mission to Boost Innovation: Shri Piyush Goyal

Shri Piyush Goyal Urges Early Investment in Deep-Tech Startups, Calls for Faster Commercialisation of Indian Innovation

29 JUL 2026 9:19PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, today said that India's future growth would depend on innovation, deep technologies, skilled manpower, startups, MSMEs and an enabling policy environment that encourages enterprise and investment, supported by globally competitive manufacturing, good manufacturing practices and uncompromising quality standards across sectors.

Delivering the 22nd J.R.D. Tata Memorial Lecture on the occasion of the 122nd birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna Shri Jehangir Ratanji Dadabhoy (J.R.D.) Tata in New Delhi today, the Minister said India's journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047 would be driven by technology, research and development, entrepreneurship and a culture of excellence.

Shri Goyal said emerging and deep technologies, including artificial intelligence, semiconductors, quantum computing, biotechnology, robotics and advanced materials, will define the next frontier of industrial growth and strengthen India's industrial capabilities. He said the Government is committed to strengthening startups, promoting MSMEs, encouraging deep technology innovation and expanding skill development initiatives. He emphasised that skill development cannot be a government-led effort alone and must become an industry-led movement, while the Government will continue improving ease of doing business and creating an enabling ecosystem in which enterprises can grow and compete globally.

Highlighting several Government initiatives aimed at promoting research and innovation, Shri Goyal said the Government has launched a ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Fund to provide long-term, low-cost risk capital for emerging technologies and innovation. He further stated that under the IndiaAI Mission, nearly 38,000 GPUs have already been onboarded to provide affordable computing capacity to startups and researchers, with plans for further expansion. He also highlighted the success of the India Semiconductor Mission, stating that commitments have already been received for the entire allocation under the first phase. He added that the Government has now launched the second Semiconductor Mission with an allocation of approximately US$12-13 billion and invited industry to participate through new investments and proposals.

Shri Goyal said innovation and manufacturing must progress together. He emphasised that the future of manufacturing lies in producing smarter through technology, automation, better product design, improved packaging, stronger branding and globally competitive quality. While India's large domestic market provides economies of scale, he said Indian industry must increasingly leverage that scale to expand into global markets, generating higher growth, creating more employment opportunities and maximising the benefits arising from India's expanding network of Free Trade Agreements.

Referring to India's Free Trade Agreement (FTA) strategy, Shri Goyal said the country has concluded nine FTAs covering 38 developed economies with a combined GDP of nearly US$60 trillion. He contrasted these agreements with India's earlier FTAs concluded prior to 2014, which were largely with economies having a combined GDP of around US$10 trillion and where India competed rather than complemented partner countries. He said these agreements provide Indian businesses with unprecedented market access and opportunities for expansion, adding that J.R.D. Tata's emphasis on quality and perfection would have enabled him to leverage such opportunities on a massive scale.

Highlighting India's economic performance, Shri Goyal said the country recorded economic growth of 7.7 per cent last year and 7.8 per cent in the last quarter, maintaining its position as the world's fastest-growing large economy despite global disruptions and geopolitical uncertainties. He said India's exports of both goods and services continued to grow during 2025-26 despite prolonged geopolitical tensions, uncertainties relating to crude oil and gas supplies, developments affecting the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, and the imposition of 50 per cent tariffs on most Indian exports to the United States for a substantial part of the previous year. He added that merchandise exports have grown by 15 per cent during the current financial year from 1 April till date, demonstrating the resilience of the Indian economy. Shri Goyal said institutions such as the OECD, World Bank and IMF continue to project India as the fastest-growing large economy, attributing this confidence to India's enabling policy environment, the self-belief of its people, the entrepreneurial spirit of young Indians and the country's emergence as the world's third-largest startup ecosystem.

Continuing his address, Shri Goyal said created advantage matters more than inherited advantage and that India's future competitiveness would be determined by its ability to innovate.

The Minister said India's startup ecosystem has evolved significantly from its initial phase and is now increasingly focused on deep technology.

Recalling his participation alongside Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and French President Emmanuel Macron at the inauguration of Bharat Innovates in Nice, France, on 14 June, Shri Goyal said 120 of India's leading deep-tech startups showcased their innovations before global investors, technology companies and world leaders. He said every participant returned with a renewed sense of confidence and pride after witnessing the quality of Indian innovation.

Shri Goyal stressed that the next priority should be to help startups move from ideas to prototypes and from prototypes to commercialisation. He urged industry to support startups by adopting their products, experimenting with their technologies and helping them scale commercially. Once proof of concept evolves into commercial success, he said, global markets would naturally follow.

Expressing concern over the loss of promising Indian innovations to overseas investors, Shri Goyal said many of the country's best technologies and startups are eventually acquired by foreign companies because Indian investors often wait until businesses mature before investing. He urged domestic investors to support Indian startups at an early stage and said India's deep-tech entrepreneurs represent an enormous investment opportunity. Referring to the 120 startups that participated in Bharat Innovates, he remarked that, had he been in business instead of public life, he would have invested his savings in such innovators.

The Minister said India's economy, currently valued at approximately US$4 trillion, is well positioned to achieve its stated target of US$13 trillion by 2047, when the country celebrates 100 years of Independence. He said India is already witnessing examples of this transformation across sectors.

Highlighting major reform initiatives, Shri Goyal said the Government has reduced compliance burden, decriminalised numerous legal provisions through the Jan Vishwas Acts, removed several obsolete laws from the statute books and continues to simplify regulations to encourage enterprise. He said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is working every day to remove the barriers that constrain entrepreneurship and unlock the true potential of Indian industry.

The Minister said that over the past decade, equal emphasis has been placed on strengthening India's macroeconomic fundamentals and expanding public welfare through technology-enabled governance. He said direct benefit transfers have ensured that welfare reaches beneficiaries without leakages or intermediaries, while sustained efforts have been made to provide every citizen with basic necessities including food, housing, electricity, water, healthcare, education, physical connectivity and digital connectivity.

He also underscored the importance of MSMEs in India's development journey and said the sector must be supported in adopting technology at scale to improve productivity, competitiveness and product quality.

Shri Goyal said that while policies, incentives and technology provide the necessary framework for development, the ultimate success of every reform depends upon the people who implement it. He observed that the rise of a nation is determined not only by the quality of its policies but also by the quality of its mindset and national character.

Recalling the legacy of J.R.D. Tata, Shri Goyal said that he did not merely build companies but built capabilities, confidence and a spirit of self-belief in India. Referring to Guru Purnima, which is also observed on 29 July, the Minister said that, in the Indian tradition, a Guru removes doubts and transfers capability to students, adding that J.R.D. Tata played exactly that role for Indian industry.

Concluding his address, Shri Goyal urged Indian industry to pursue excellence by aiming for perfection and making the "Made in India" label synonymous with global respect and uncompromising quality. He appealed to industry to reinvest earnings in research and development, innovation, skill development, education and nation building. He also urged businesses to leverage India's Free Trade Agreements to expand their global market share and called upon industry to invest boldly in deep technologies, including artificial intelligence, quantum computing, biotechnology and the space sector, while continuously innovating within their own businesses.

headline: Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda calls upon MPs from West Bengal to lead Jan Andolan for TB Elimination
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda calls upon MPs from West Bengal to lead Jan Andolan for TB Elimination

Says India has recorded a 21% decline in TB incidence, nearly double the global pace, with a treatment coverage rate of 92%

Urges Members of Parliament to strengthen community participation, early detection and district-level monitoring to achieve TB elimination by 2030

Highlights indigenous innovations, AI-enabled diagnostics and enhanced patient support as key drivers of India's TB elimination journey

29 JUL 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Health & Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today chaired a meeting titled "Parliamentarians Championing a TB Mukt Bharat" with Members of Parliament from West Bengal on the sidelines of the Monsoon Session of Parliament at the Extended Parliament House Annexe, New Delhi. He was joined by Union Minister of State for Education & Development of North Eastern Region, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar.

The meeting brought together Members of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha from West Bengal across party lines to strengthen collective efforts towards achieving a TB Mukt Bharat through greater political leadership and community participation.

The meeting was part of a series of sensitisation interactions chaired by the Union Health Minister with Members of Parliament from states across the country, including Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and others. Shri Nadda informed the Members that similar consultations have been held with MPs from other States as well, as part of the Government's whole-of-government approach to accelerate TB elimination.

The meeting reviewed the progress made under the 100-Day TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, implemented in two phases to accelerate India's efforts towards TB elimination. The first phase, launched on 7th December 2024, initially covered 347 high-priority districts before being expanded nationwide and concluded on 24th March 2025. The second phase, launched on 24th March 2026, focused on nearly 1.58 lakh high-risk villages and urban wards across the country.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda described the campaign as "a defining moment in the nation's fight against tuberculosis, built on innovation, compassion and unwavering political will." He reiterated that the principal objective of the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is to achieve the Sustainable Development Goal of eliminating tuberculosis by 2030.

Highlighting India's remarkable progress, Shri Nadda cited the WHO Global TB Report 2025 and stated that India has recorded a 21% decline in TB incidence between 2015 and 2024, compared to the global average decline of 12%, making India's pace of decline nearly twice the global average. He further noted that India's treatment coverage rate has reached 92%, significantly higher than the global average of 78%, reflecting the country's leadership in global TB control efforts.

The Union Health Minister emphasized that TB Mukt Bharat is not merely a health programme but a nationwide people's movement requiring active public participation. Stressing the importance of Jan Bhagidari, he said that the campaign can achieve its full potential only through collective ownership involving elected representatives, governments, civil society and communities.

Calling upon Members of Parliament to lead this movement in their constituencies, Shri Nadda urged them to:

Regularly review TB elimination efforts with District Collectors/District Magistrates and the Health Department.

Intensify awareness generation and stigma reduction while promoting early detection through Ni-kshay Shivirs and screening of high-risk villages and vulnerable populations, including asymptomatic TB cases.

Strengthen oversight of TB programme implementation and service delivery through visits to district and block-level health facilities.

Encourage community participation by mobilising Ni-kshay Mitras and local organisations to provide nutritional, psychosocial and livelihood support to TB patients.

Organise targeted Ayushman Arogya Shivirs to proactively screen high-risk and vulnerable populations.

Highlighting India's transformative TB elimination journey, Shri Nadda underscored the importance of universal mandatory notification of TB cases diagnosed in the private sector, alongside the provision of free government-supplied medicines to reduce the financial burden on patients.

The Union Health Minister described the proactive detection of asymptomatic TB cases as a revolutionary step in the country's TB elimination strategy. He highlighted the role of indigenous TruNat molecular diagnostic machines in detecting Multi-Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and noted that AI-enabled handheld X-ray machines have significantly improved access to early diagnosis in remote and underserved areas. He added that portable X-ray units supported through PM CARES are further expanding doorstep diagnostic services across the country.

Shri Nadda also highlighted the Government's patient-centric initiatives, including enhancement of the monthly nutritional support under the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana to ₹1,000 per patient, introduction of shorter and advanced treatment regimens, and the mobilisation of over 5 lakh Ni-kshay Mitras nationwide to provide sustained nutritional and social support to TB patients.

In his concluding remarks, Shri Nadda commended the parliamentarians for their commitment and expressed confidence that West Bengal has the potential to emerge as a leader in TB elimination. He observed that while the 100-Day Campaign has concluded, the real measure of success will lie in sustained progress across every district.

Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava highlighted that West Bengal’s continued expansion of screening, treatment and patient support would be crucial in translating national progress into community-level impact.

Additional Secretary and Mission Director, National Health Mission, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, highlighted the technological backbone of India's TB elimination programme. She noted that molecular testing capacity has expanded from a few hundred machines a decade ago to more than 9,000 today, complemented by nearly 3,000 AI-enabled handheld X-ray units developed through indigenous innovation to ensure timely diagnosis across the country.

Presenting West Bengal's performance across key indicators, she highlighted the state's progress in TB notifications, treatment success, preventive therapy coverage and alignment with national elimination targets. During the 100-Day Campaign, West Bengal implemented focused strategies by taking Ayushman Arogya Shivirs to urban slums, tea gardens, mining sites and migrant settlements, thereby bringing screening and care closer to vulnerable populations.

The Members of Parliament from West Bengal collectively reaffirmed their commitment to intensifying awareness campaigns, reducing stigma, organising Ni-kshay Shivirs for early detection among vulnerable populations, strengthening oversight of TB services at district and block levels, and mobilising communities under the Jan Andolan through greater participation of Ni-kshay Mitras and local organisations to provide nutritional, psychosocial and livelihood support to TB patients.

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW  
Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda convened a meeting with West Bengal Members of Parliament on 29 July 2026 to review progress under the 100‑Day TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan and to call upon MPs to spearhead a nationwide Jan Andolan for tuberculosis elimination by 2030.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS  
- **Meeting details:** 29 July 2026, Monsoon Session Annex, New Delhi; chaired by the Health Minister, joined by Union Minister of State for Education & Development of the North Eastern Region, Dr. .."**; involved West Bengal MPs across party lines.  
- **Series of consultations:** part of a nationwide effort with MPs from Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat atualização, Rajasthan, Roof, ... (Melave).  
- **100‑Day TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan:**  
  - *Phase 1:* 7 Dec 2024 – 24 Mar 2025; initially 347 high‑priority districts, later expanded nationwide.  
  - *Phase 2:* launched 24 Mar 2026; targets ~1.58 lakh high‑risk villages and urban wards.  
- **National TB metrics (WHO Global TB Report 2025):**  
  - 21 % decline in TB incidence (2015‑2024) versus a global 12 % decline.  
  - Treatment coverage reached 92 % versus a global average of 78 %.  
- **Key actions requested from MPs:**  
  - Regularly review progress with district authorities.  
  - Intensify awareness, stigma reduction, and early detection via Ni‑kshay Shivirs and high‑risk screenings.  
  - Strengthen oversight of district and block‑level service delivery.  
  - Mobilise Ni‑kshay Mitras and local NGOs to provide nutrition, psychosocial and livelihood support.  
  - Organise targeted Ayushman Arogya Shivirs for high‑risk and vulnerable populations.  
- **Innovation and technology initiatives:**  
  - Indigenous TruNat molecular diagnostics for MDR‑TB.  
  - AI‑enabled handheld X‑ray machines (~3,000 units) improving access in remote areas.  
  - Portable X‑ray units supported through PM CARES expanding doorstep diagnostics.  
- **Patient‑centred measures:**  
  - Monthly nutritional support under Ni‑kshay Poshan Yojana increased to ₹1,000 per patient.  
  - Introduction of shorter and advanced treatment regimens.  
  - Mobilised > 5 lakh Ni‑kshay Mitras across the country.  
- **West Bengal performance indicators:**  
  - Enhanced screening in urban slums, tea gardens, mining sites, and migrant settlements.  
  - Improved TB notifications, treatment success, and preventive therapy coverage, aligning with national elimination targets.

headline: DAANVEER Initiative Launched; To Boost Digital Infrastructure Across India's Gram Panchayats
fullText:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj

DAANVEER Initiative Launched; To Boost Digital Infrastructure Across India's Gram Panchayats

Citizens can Voluntarily Contribute Computers to Gram Panchayats through Meri Panchayat App

DAANVEER makes citizens active partners in building Digital India" : Shri Vivek Bharadwaj

29 JUL 2026 7:55PM by PIB Delhi

DAANVEER, a citizen participation initiative to strengthen the digital infrastructure of Gram Panchayats across the country was launched today by Shri Vivek Bharadwaj, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj in New Delhi. DAANVEER is a platform designed not just to close the immediate computer gap in the Gram Panchayats but to evolve into a long-term, citizen-powered ecosystem for strengthening local institutions. It is a transparent, end-to-end digital and verifiable platform that enables citizens and organisations to contribute towards the identified technology and infrastructure needs of Gram Panchayats in India. The initiative institutionalises the spirit of voluntarism in the society by providing a structured, accountable and seamless mechanism for supporting grassroots digital infrastructure. An initiative of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, it has been developed in collaboration with the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and DigiHaat.

View this post on Instagram

Launching the initiative, Shri Vivek Bharadwaj described DAANVEER as an important step towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat by ensuring that every Gram Panchayat is digitally equipped, connected and future-ready. He said that the initiative provides citizens across the globe, with an opportunity to reconnect with their roots by contributing meaningfully to the development of their native villages. Emphasising upon the transformative role of digital infrastructure at the grassroots, he observed that a computer in a Gram Panchayat is no longer merely a device for maintaining records; it is an enabler of faster service delivery, greater transparency and improved governance. He noted that DAANVEER should be viewed not as a donation drive, but as a platform for partnership that enables citizens and institutions to become active participants in strengthening local self-governance and advancing the vision of Digital India.

The State officials participating in the event from Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra lauded the initiative and shared that several citizens and philanthropists in their respective States have already shown keen interest in supporting Gram Panchayats by donating computers. They noted that strengthening digital infrastructure at the Panchayat level would significantly improve the efficiency, transparency and accessibility of public service delivery in the country.

The launch was also attended by Smt. Mukta Shekhar, Joint Secretary MoPR; Smt. Palka Sahni, Joint Secretary MoPR; Shri Vipul Ujwal, Director MoPR along with senior officials from the State Panchayati Raj Departments from Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.

DAANVEER builds upon India’s long tradition of voluntary public contribution while introducing a technology-enabled institutional framework to enhance trust, transparency and ease of participation. Drawing on the experience of earlier voluntary contribution models, the initiative incorporates verified institutional needs, standardised contribution options, end-to-end digital tracking, and direct delivery, thereby creating a credible standardized mechanism through which citizens can participate in strengthening public institutions. Carrying the tagline “Give Back to Your Village”, DAANVEER is entirely voluntary. Available through the Meri Panchayat mobile application, DAANVEER enables individuals and organisations to contribute standardized, quality-verified computer bundles directly to eligible Gram Panchayats. The initiative integrates the Meri Panchayat app with the DigiHaat marketplace, allowing donors to choose from pre-approved computer bundles that are mapped to State-specific technical specifications. Delivery details are automatically populated, eliminating additional paperwork. Donors can also track their contribution from dispatch to installation and receive a digital certificate of appreciation in recognition of their support. Details of the initiative, including the list of eligible Gram Panchayats and the contribution process, are available through the Meri Panchayat app.

India has nearly 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats, which form the foundation of grassroots democracy and local service delivery. Building on the Ministry’s digital governance ecosystem-including e-GramSwaraj, Meri Panchayat, Sabha Saar, AuditOnline, Gram Manchitra and other digital platforms – DAANVEER seeks to bridge digital infrastructure gaps and ensure that every Gram Panchayat is equipped to deliver citizen-centric services efficiently and transparently. The initiative also provides citizens living away from their native villages, including members of the Indian diaspora, with a credible and transparent mechanism to contribute to the development of the Gram Panchayats to which they remain connected. Through DAANVEER, citizens can meaningfully participate in strengthening rural digital infrastructure while contributing to the broader vision of a digitally empowered and self-reliant rural India.

headline: Shri Tokhan Sahu Visits HFA Division, Appreciates Team's Contribution Towards Realising the Vision of 'Housing for All'
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

Shri Tokhan Sahu Visits HFA Division, Appreciates Team's Contribution Towards Realising the Vision of 'Housing for All'

Over 127 Lakh Houses Sanctioned Under PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0; More Than 99 Lakh Completed and Over 96 Lakh Families Housed Nationwide

29 JUL 2026 7:47PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Tokhan Sahu, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, reaffirming his commitment to engaging with the teams implementing the Ministry's flagship programmes, today paid a visit to the Housing for All (HFA) Division at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi.

During the visit, Shri Sahu, accompanied by Shri Kuldip Narayan, Joint Secretary (HFA & Housing), and Shri R. K. Gautam, Deputy Director General (HFA), walked through different sections of the HFA Division and interacted with officials, consultants, young professionals and support staff at their workstations to gain first-hand insights into the Division's functioning. He held discussions with teams implementing PMAY-U 2.0, reviewing ongoing priorities, key initiatives and the progress of the Mission. He also listened to suggestions from the teams, appreciated their dedicated efforts in ensuring the timely and effective delivery of affordable housing to eligible urban beneficiaries, and acknowledged their invaluable contribution towards advancing one of the Government's most transformative urban missions.

Shri Sahu also reviewed the PMAY-U Monitoring Dashboard, which provides a comprehensive overview of the Mission's progress through digital monitoring systems. Appreciating the use of technology and data-driven governance in improving transparency, accountability and real-time monitoring, he encouraged the team to continue adopting innovative approaches to make the implementation of the Mission more efficient and citizen-centric.

Commending the dedicated efforts of the HFA Division, Shri Sahu noted that the Ministry has so far sanctioned over 127 lakh houses under PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0 , including more than 16 lakh houses under PMAY-U 2.0. Of these, over 121 lakh houses have been grounded, more than 99 lakh houses have been completed, and over 96 lakh families have already moved into their homes across the country.

Addressing the HFA team, Shri Sahu said, "These remarkable achievements are a testament to the unwavering dedication, professionalism and commitment of every member of the HFA Division. Behind every completed house is a family whose life has been transformed. You are not merely building homes; you are creating opportunities, restoring dignity, providing security, and giving millions of citizens the foundation for a better future."

Emphasising the inclusive nature of PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, Shri Sahu highlighted that the Mission has empowered some of the most vulnerable sections of society. Of the total houses sanctioned, more than 21 lakh beneficiaries belong to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category, over 5 lakh to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category, and nearly 50 lakh to the Other Backward Classes (OBC). Additionally, more than 22 lakh beneficiaries belong to minority communities, while over one crore houses have been sanctioned in the name of women or under joint ownership with male members of their families, reinforcing the Government's commitment to women's empowerment, social equity and financial security.

Shri Sahu said that these achievements reflect the Government's steadfast commitment to ensuring that the benefits of development reach every section of society. He noted that PMAY-U 2.0 has emerged as a powerful instrument of social inclusion and empowerment, translating the vision of "Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas" into reality under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Sharing his experiences from visits across various States and Union Territories, Shri Sahu recalled the heartfelt interactions he had with PMAY-U beneficiaries. He said that listening to the stories of families who had realised their dream of owning a pucca house reinforced the transformative impact of the Mission.

"Whenever I visit different parts of the country, I meet beneficiaries whose lives have been transformed through PMAY-U. Their smiles and stories remind us that our work is touching millions of lives. I congratulate every officer, consultant and staff member of the HFA Division for their invaluable contribution towards this national mission and encourage them to continue working with the same dedication and commitment," Shri Sahu said.

Concluding his visit Shri Sahu reiterated that PMAY-U 2.0 will continue to play a pivotal role in providing affordable housing to eligible urban families while strengthening the Government's commitment to inclusive urban development and the vision of a Viksit Bharat.
